text: Can you explain what LoRA does differently from full fine-tuning, and when I'd actually want to use it?
label: general
rationale: A concept question (Stage 3 intent: concept). LoRA (Hu et al., 2021, arXiv 2106.09685) is widely discussed in blogs, docs and papers before any plausible training cutoff, and the answer (freeze pretrained weights, inject trainable low-rank matrices; use it when GPU memory or storing many fine-tuned copies is the constraint) needs no external fact. The model should answer this correctly from parametric knowledge alone; the catalogue abstract for 2106.09685 is the student's check.

text: Who wrote the original ResNet paper and what year did it come out?
label: general
rationale: A paper fact about one canonical paper (Stage 3 intent: paper_lookup). 'Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition' by Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren and Jian Sun (2015) is one of the most cited papers in ML, so the author list and year are stable, heavily repeated facts the model knows from training data. Ground truth is in data/papers.json under 1512.03385 (v1, published 2015-12-10).

text: How many citations does 'Attention Is All You Need' have on Semantic Scholar right now?
label: needs_data
rationale: A live number that changes every day. Anything the model says is at best a stale figure from its training window and at worst a confident round-number invention; it has no way to query Semantic Scholar. Correct behaviour in Stage 1 is to say it cannot know; Stage 4 fixes it with a tool that calls the Semantic Scholar API for arXiv:1706.03762. Record whether the model admits uncertainty or just states a number.

text: Which papers in my saved catalogue are about LLM agents or tool use, and how many papers do I have in it in total?
label: needs_data
rationale: Needs the local catalogue data/papers.json, which the model has never seen. Ground truth: 23 papers in total; clear agent/tool-use hits are ReAct (2210.03629), Toolformer (2302.04761) and Reflexion (2303.11366); Tree of Thoughts (2305.10601) and Chain-of-Thought (2201.11903) are reasoning-method papers, borderline at most. Any confident list or count from the model is invented.

text: What's the exact arXiv id and latest version number of the Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes paper by Kingma and Welling?
label: needs_data
rationale: A precise metadata fact (Stage 3 intent: paper_lookup). The model has probably memorised the id 1312.6114 because the paper is famous, but the version counter is an obscure, changing arXiv detail: the catalogue records v11, which the model will almost certainly guess wrong (v1 or v2) while sounding sure. This separates 'knows the paper' from 'knows the record' and is answered in Stage 4 by get_paper reading data/papers.json or the arXiv API.

label: memory
rationale: First half of the tutorial's two-run memory probe. Run it as its own graph.invoke. The Stage 1 graph has no checkpointer or thread_id, so the state (and this message) lives only inside this single invocation; the model will acknowledge the name, which looks fine on its own. This run exists to set up item 7.

label: memory
rationale: Second half of the memory probe, run as a separate graph.invoke. Nothing carries over between invocations in Stage 1, so the model cannot know the name and should say so (or, worse, invent one). This is the persistence failure the tutorial says you return to in later stages (checkpointer and thread_id, then long-term memory); record it in the Stage 1 results table next to the three needs_data failures.
